newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi Arabia reviewing foreign investment rules.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia reviewing foreign investment rules.

text.p: Saudi Arabia is reviewing its foreign capital law to introduce more incentives to international investors, Saudi Industry and Electricity Minister Hashem bin Abdullah bin Hashem Yamani said.

"The kingdom is trying to review the foreign investment rule to come up with a new rule that will provide more incentives to create an encouraging investment environment for foreign capital," he added.
Yamani was speaking at a two-day investment seminar which ended on Wednesday in the eastern city of Dammam to discuss industrial investment opportunities in the kingdom.
The world's biggest oil producer and exporter is trying to reduce government's dominant role and diversify its economy.

Most foreign capital invested in the kingdom is in joint ventures with Saudi firms. Foreign capital can be invested without Saudi participation, but then it does not qualify for a range of incentives, including tax holidays.
"There are big challenges ahead of us. Competition with global production is expected and we have to be prepared for that," Yamani said.
At the seminar, 16 new project opportunities in Saudi Arabia were identified, requiring total investment of two billion riyals ($533 million).
"Sixteen new investment opportunities are available in various industrial sectors," Council of Saudi Chambers of Commerce chairman Hamad al-Zamel told the seminar.
Zamel, also president of the Eastern Province Chamber of Commerce, said the new projects included those in the chemical, petrochemical, plastic, minerals, construction and food sectors.
The Doha-based Gulf Organisation for Industrial Consulting (GOIC) prepared the project proposals.
GOIC head Abdul-Rahman al-Jaafari said the Gulf Arab states needed to invest at least $1.5 billion a year in the manufacturing sector in the next 30 years.
"Our estimation in the GOIC indicates the manufacturing sector needs investment of at least $1.5 billion annually until the year 2025 to keep pace with current labour growth."

Annual population growth in Saudi Arabia is estimated at three to four percent. King Fahd has urged the private sector to employ more nationals and said the government will ensure that 650,000 Saudis have private sector jobs by the year 2000.
